steps.text: A **training block** is a plan you can test: a **goal** (one specific thing), **practice** (what, how often, how long), a **baseline** (a measure before you start) and a **later check on tasks you did not practise**. Plans can fail, and a failed plan that you measured teaches more than a plan you never tested.

steps.prompt: Choose one goal for a block. Use your error log or unsure moments as evidence, not a feeling.

fields.label: The evidence it matters (games, log entries):

steps.text: In a real block, practice runs for days with many positions. Here it is compressed: one practice position, then a check position that is new. The baseline above was your first attempt at the same skill, answering the opponent's last move.

steps.title: A fair check
steps.prompt: Two positions could be used as the check. One is new; one is the practice position flipped left to right. Which makes a fair check?

steps.text: **Revise from evidence.** At the check date compare with the baseline. Then change one thing: keep the plan, change the practice, or change the goal. If the check is no better than the baseline, the plan may be wrong, the check may be too noisy, or the block too short. With a few items you cannot tell which; say so.

steps.prompt: Write the block. The check must use positions or games you have not practised.

fields.label: Baseline: how I will measure before starting:
What result would make me change the plan?

steps.text: **What the app does for you now, and when it stops.** Now it gives you the template, a baseline item and check items from families you have not practised. The plan is that you choose the block length and write your own check, and the app only keeps the check items sealed until your check date. Silent practice: do your block with the app closed and return on the date.

steps.prompt: Revision, to fill in at the check date. Compare with your baseline and change one thing.

fields.label: The one thing I will change:
Could the plan have failed because of the plan, the check, or the length of the block?
